title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-29
lineage: SBD > MR > CD > EAC > Cool Edit > CD Wave > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a fire‑filled Fillmore East night with a smoking Hard to Handle, monster Alligator jam and soaring Morning Dew.
ai_review.review: The recording is an A+‑grade soundboard tape that sounds as if the band were in your living room – crisp drums, clean guitars and a well‑balanced mix.  Musically the show is legendary: Hard to Handle erupts into a “musical orgasm,” the Alligator → Jam → GDTRFB sequence is often called the best of its era, and Morning Dew (plus Bird Song, Ripple and Pig Pen highlights) are in top form.  A few reviewers note occasional low‑energy moments or minor equipment hiccups, but the overwhelming consensus is that this is one of the Dead’s quintessential Fillmore East performances.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (over 80 %) award 5 stars and praise both the musical performance and the tape quality; only a handful of low‑score outliers mention availability or minor flaws.  Weighted 70 % show + 30 % recording yields an overall rating in the excellent range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers call the tape "clean," "A+" or "crisp"; mentions of a flawless mix, clear drum solo and superb guitar tone.  One comment notes minor equipment glitches but they do not detract from overall clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A marathon second set packed with seamless transitions – Hard to Handle kicks off a high‑octane run that flows into the Alligator jam, then GDTRFB, Cold Rain & Snow and later Bird Song; the first set provides solid roots material (Truckin', Pig Pen tunes) leading into an explosive finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone and solos are repeatedly praised – especially on Hard to Handle, Morning Dew and during the Alligator jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh is lauded for "bombs" on bass throughout the Alligator‑Jam‑GDTRFB sequence and on Sugar Magnolia; his low‑end foundation gets special mention.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pig Pen’s vocal grit and harmonica work are highlighted as “best” on this night, particularly in Pig Pen numbers and the Alligator jam.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drum solo is described as intimate and crystal‑clear; his steady groove underpins the lengthy jams.
